cases.q: What has he done for accessibility?
cases.answer: Craig has built UI libraries held to WCAG standards for clients. His current site is held to WCAG 2.2 AA, utilizing an automated suite that checks the site after every deploy and every week to prevent regressions, as detailed in accessibility.md. This suite uses axe-core to check every automated rule in every state across 244 page states per run. His accessibility work includes ensuring keyboard-only navigation with visible focus rings, managing reflow and spacing so nothing scrolls sideways at 320px, and providing motion control for reduced-motion users. He also ensures controls meet minimum target sizes and that single-key shortcuts can be switched off to avoid clashing with screen readers.

Yes, Craig remains a skilled, hands-on engineer. While he sets strategy and leads teams, he has upskilled in AI-assisted development and maintains recent pull requests on his site. He is interested in hands-on technical leadership roles, such as Head of Engineering, where he can stay close to the code and AI-first delivery.
